title: Obesity, morbid obesity and BMI
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's weight diagnosis and BMI, if reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for weight management.

HPI
The patient is a 52-year-old male presenting today for a follow-up evaluation regarding his weight and overall health management. He reports that he has been attempting to incorporate more physical activity into his daily routine but finds it difficult to maintain consistency due to joint discomfort. He notes that his diet has been inconsistent over the last few months, often consuming high-calorie meals due to a busy work schedule. He expresses a desire to lose weight to improve his general mobility and reduce the strain on his knees. He denies any recent acute injuries or significant changes in his baseline health status.

Medication List
Lisinopril 20mg daily
Atorvastatin 40mg daily
Multivitamin daily

Review of Systems
The patient reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He denies any recent fevers, chills, or night sweats. He denies any significant headaches or dizzy spells. He reports mild bilateral knee pain but denies any acute swelling or redness.

Social History
The patient works full-time in a sedentary office environment. He reports a sedentary lifestyle outside of work and notes that he enjoys watching sports on weekends. He denies tobacco use and reports occasional alcohol consumption.

Family History
His father had hypertension and suffered a myocardial infarction at age 65. His mother has type 2 diabetes and osteoarthritis.

Vitals
BP: 132/84 mmHg
HR: 78 bpm
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on room air
Height: 5'10"
Weight: 282 lbs
BMI: 37.6

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 5.8%
eGFR: 82 mL/min/1.73m2
LDL: 95 mg/dL

Exam
The patient is a well-groomed male in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented x3. He appears to be in no acute pain. Physical examination reveals a BMI of 37.6. He has symmetrical muscle strength in all extremities. No new skin lesions or rashes are noted. Cardiovascular and respiratory exams are unremarkable.

Assessment
The patient presents with morbid obesity. He is currently making progress with his medications but requires more structured intervention for weight reduction.

Plan
We discussed the importance of caloric deficit and increased physical activity. I have provided a referral to a formal weight management program for structured nutritional counseling. The patient will begin a walking program aiming for 30 minutes, five days a week. We will follow up in three months to monitor progress and laboratory values.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Morbid (severe) obesity documented by the provider: E66.01 (HCC 48).
BMI 37.x with a provider weight diagnosis: add Z68.37.

distractors.why: The provider documents morbid obesity: E66.01, not E66.9.
The BMI is documented and the provider diagnosed the weight condition: add the Z68 code.
